C1 diffeomorphism plus positive Jacobian preserves null exceptions under inverse, so coefficient bounds pull back a.e. Finite measurable partition and L2 gradients allow cell/global Cauchy-Schwarz; implemented density is L1 as exact density minus integrable defect. For stability, singular values <= L with product >= j_- give inverse norm <= L^(d-1)/j_- and J <= L^d, hence the stated (loose but valid) B bound Lambda L^(3d-2)/j_-^2. Beta=j_- lambda/L^2 and eta<=beta/2 give coercivity. Completeness of gradient norm is explicitly assumed on Z_h, not inferred; partition nonempty, zero functions and eta=0 work. No rate without the independent cellwise assumption.

On strict positive-width cells, n=1 midpoint error is h_K^3 ||A''|| infinity |v_K' w_K'| /24; factoring sqrt(h_K) twice and finite Cauchy-Schwarz yields h^2/24 globally. Essential supremum equals maximum for continuous A''. Zero slopes, one cell and affine coefficient give the expected zero errors; no roundoff claim. Checked the actual unchanged example and all direct suppliers. V=V_h has ordered basis phi, coefficient inner product and complete finite-dimensional norm. Power rule and FTC give integral (1-2x)^2=1/3, hence exact boundedness and coercivity 1/3 in that norm. One midpoint panel has admissible a=0,b=1,n=1 and returns zero since phi'(1/2)=0. Reviewed the full H1 error budget against the already-reviewed interpolation, Poincare, midpoint-defect and first-Strang suppliers, plus the actual Sobolev Hilbert supplier. Holder and finite Cauchy-Schwarz prove exact/discrete bounds M; sampled positivity gives alpha/2 coercivity, without any smallness condition. Interpolant belongs to V_h by hypothesis, so its H1 error <=sqrt(2)h||u''|| infinity and slope norm <=||u'||2+h||u''|| infinity. Form defect and load defect enter with factor 2/alpha, yielding every displayed constant. Added F(v)=a(u,v), real scalar/load conventions and the framework zero-space defect convention. These make the Statement match A1 and the proof. Checked current moment datum, monic orthogonal polynomial, Gauss rule and exactness supplier statements against m=2,r=3 and Lebesgue measure restricted to Borel subsets of [-1,1]. Positive interval measure gives full relative support and at least three points; bounded polynomial moments through degree three satisfy the weaker moment interface. Orthogonality to 1 and x gives c=-1/3 and b=0 using moments 2,0,2/3,0; roots are distinct interior nodes +/-1/sqrt(3), cardinal polynomials integrate to unit weights. Exactness applies through degree three; the separate fourth moment is directly finite and FTC plus Riemann/Lebesgue agreement gives integral x^4=2/5 versus Q=2/9, error 8/45. Explicit Countable Choice supplies measure and integral bridge. Opened Rutgers Lecture14 PDF, printed p44 sections10.3-10.4 and Theorem11, and p45 example; citation locator and numerical rule match. No need for a squared-norm order-four moment assumption to construct the order-three rule. No logical consumers of this example.
